answer: Yes. Through the live session workspace broker, a write from one session into another session's worktree or artifact root is denied with code SESS_CROSS_SESSION_WRITE and an alert that names both session ids; an independent pre/post sha256 of the victim tree is unchanged; a write inside the actor's own session root succeeds in the same run; the deny was observed while a second session process was genuinely alive under /proc.

evidence.claim: A cross-session worktree write is refused with SESS_CROSS_SESSION_WRITE. The denial alert names both actor_session_id and victim_session_id.

Independent pre/post sha256 of the victim session worktree and artifact root is unchanged after the denied write; oob_path_exists is false for the planted payload. An unmediated Path.write_bytes of the same payload does change the hash, so the probe is not vacuously green.
Both-states control: a write inside the actor's own worktree and artifact root succeeds in the same run.

Concurrency: the victim session is a live OS process (/proc/<pid> present) with a heartbeat file outside the hashed tree while the cross-session write is attempted. Reviewer bypasses (relative traversal and symlink hop) are also denied with alerts naming both session ids.

negative_controls.description: A write into another session's worktree is denied AND a write inside the actor's own session root succeeds in the same run. A blanket deny would fail the own-write half; a missing gate would fail the cross-session half.
A write performed without the broker does create the file and changes the victim tree hash, proving the denied-write test is not vacuously passing because the write was never attempted.

question_or_target: Is cross-session write containment enforced, given multiple concurrent agent sessions on this box? PASS requires a denied write plus an alert naming both session ids.

residual_unknowns.claim: This unit enforces the in-process session workspace broker. Cursor/IDE Write tool calls that never enter tools/lib/workspace.py, and OS-level sandboxing (Landlock/seccomp), are residual. tools/lib/workspace.mjs is present as a workspace-root detector, not this broker.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Hook the broker at the agent Write tool boundary, or an ADV escape probe that writes via a path that never calls SessionBroker.write_file.

retry.policy: no automatic retry: a failure here is a finding, not a transient
